findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/graph/README.md (lines 1-8, 51, 122-133) still documents the DELETED standalone-binary concept as current: it tells a reader to invoke `proof-or-stop-graph` directly (package.json has no `bin` field anymore, and packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts never calls packages/graph/src/shells/cli/main.ts -- it imports dist/index.js as a library), the Architecture section still labels shells/cli/main.ts as "the proof-or-stop-graph command", the "Migration into Proof-or-Stop" section speaks of the migration in the future tense with the wrong tentative command name `proof_graph` (the chosen name is bare `graph`) even though the migration is this story, and the Development section instructs `npm start` to "run the CLI from dist/" even though no `start` script exists in packages/graph/package.json. CHK-006 explicitly promised "grep for stale wording afterwards"; scripts/verify-docs.mjs only checks CLAUDE.md and the decisions doc, never packages/graph/README.md, so this stale content shipped uncaught. The file is shipped in the published package (package.json files: ["dist","assets","README.md"]) and is the first thing a developer opens under packages/graph.
findings.resolvedReason: Rewrote packages/graph/README.md in commit 235a98f8a8. The usage block now shows proof-or-stop graph and states the package has no binary of its own; the architecture table no longer labels the shell as the command; the migration section is rewritten as How the CLI reaches this package, describing the completed runtime-resolution design and pointing at docs/requirements/decisions/graph-command-migration.md; the removed npm start reference is replaced with npm run check plus the Node >= 22.5 floor. Verified: grep for proof-or-stop-graph, npm start and proof_graph in that README now returns only the cache directory name, which the reviewer separately confirmed is a legitimate internal cache key rather than binary branding.

findings.desc: packages/graph/src/shells/cli/main.ts is now dead code: packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts (the actual CLI entrypoint) resolves and imports packages/graph dist/index.js as a pure library and never invokes shells/cli/main.ts, and the package.json bin field was deliberately removed. But tsconfig.json includes src/**/* with no exclusion, so this file still compiles into dist/shells/cli/main.js, and package.json files:["dist",...] ships it inside the package tree unreachable and unreferenced. Its content (lines 3, 35-38, 57, 71) still hardcodes the removed standalone-binary name proof-or-stop-graph in its help text and error prefix (e.g. `proof-or-stop-graph: ${probe.reason}`), so if anyone stumbles on this file or its compiled output they see instructions for a binary that no longer exists. This is unreachable duplicate logic left over from the pre-migration standalone tool, not intentionally-retained back-compat (no back-compat comment present).
findings.resolvedReason: Deleted packages/graph/src/shells/cli/main.ts and its stale compiled output dist/shells/cli in commit 235a98f8a8, after confirming nothing references it: the handler consumes the package as a library through dist/index.js, the bin field was dropped, and a repo-wide grep found no caller. The user was asked and chose deletion over retaining a corrected-but-unused second entry point. The provenance comment in packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts that cited the deleted path now points at git history and the pre-migration repository instead.

findings.desc: doc-code-drift: packages/graph/README.md:1-134 still documents this package as a standalone tool invoked via bin `proof-or-stop-graph` (usage block at line 7, shells/cli description at line 51) and its "Migration into Proof-or-Stop" section (lines 121-124) frames the migration as still-future work ("would call", speculating the command would be named `proof_graph`), but this story already performed that migration: the actual entrypoint is the bare `proof-or-stop graph` command registered in packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts, packages/graph/package.json has no `bin` field so `proof-or-stop-graph` cannot be invoked at all in this repo, and packages/main now does depend on this package's library surface (createApp/startServer) via runtime resolution. A reader of this README post-migration would try the wrong command and get a wrong mental model of the naming/dependency direction that the decisions doc and CLAUDE.md correctly state. This is the exact kind of promised-vs-delivered drift the docs-review closing self-check calls out, just inverted (pre-migration prose left stale rather than a promise never implemented).
findings.resolvedReason: Duplicate of B-3e16:F-001, which the concept reviewer filed earlier in run RR-001 against the same file and the same substance (standalone bin usage plus stale future-tense migration framing). The docs reviewer noted the duplication itself. Fixed by the same README rewrite in commit 235a98f8a8; see the F-001 resolution for the verification detail.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/graph/README.md:54-56 Architecture tree still lists shells/cli/main.ts as an existing file ("standalone entry, retained from the pre-migration package (unused here -- proof-or-stop graph is the entrypoint)"), but that file was deleted in commit 235a98f8a8 (F-002 fix) and packages/graph/src/shells/ now contains only web/. This directly contradicts the same README top-of-file claim ("This package has no binary of its own", "The migration into Proof-or-Stop is complete") and the deletion commit message ("Deleted, along with its stale compiled output"). Root cause matches the note already left in that commit: verify-docs.mjs (packages/graph/scripts/verify-docs.mjs) only scans CLAUDE.md and the decisions doc, so this file is structurally outside the check meant to catch exactly this drift.
